es.summary: Lesión erosiva de la mucosa gástrica o duodenal causada por desequilibrio entre agresión ácida y defensa mucosa.
key_points: H. pylori y AINEs son las causas más frecuentes.
Dolor epigástrico típico empeora entre comidas o nocturno.
Diagnóstico: endoscopia y pruebas para H. pylori.
Tratamiento: inhibidores de bomba de protones + erradicación antibiótica.
Complicaciones graves: hemorragia, perforación y obstrucción.

pathophysiology: Exceso de ácido supera la barrera mucosa protectora.
H. pylori produce ureasa que daña epitelio y aumenta inflamación.
AINEs inhiben prostaglandinas, reducen secreción de bicarbonato y flujo sanguíneo mucoso.
Daño crónico lleva a erosión y formación de úlcera.
signs_symptoms: Dolor epigástrico ardiente, empeora entre comidas o en la noche.
Náuseas y vómitos, a veces con sangre (hematemesis).
diagnostics: Endoscopia digestiva alta: visualiza úlcera y permite biopsia.
Prueba de aliento con urea marcada para H. pylori (positiva).
Test de antígeno en heces para H. pylori.
treatment: Inhibidores de la bomba de protones: omeprazol, pantoprazol.
Antibióticos para erradicación: amoxicilina + claritromicina ± metronidazol.
Antiácidos (hidróxido de aluminio/magnesio) para alivio sintomático.
Cese de AINEs; usar acetaminofén como analgésico.
complications: Anemia crónica por pérdida de sangre.
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor (intensidad, relación con alimentos y reposo).
Monitorear signos vitales, presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca.
Controlar hemoglobina, hematocrito y signos de sangrado.
Administrar PPI según orden y observar efectos adversos.
Mantener NPO pre‑endoscopia; iniciar dieta blanda post‑procedimiento.
Posicionar al paciente semisentado para reducir reflujo.
patient_teaching: Evitar AINEs; preferir acetaminofén para dolor.
Completar el esquema antibiótico para erradicar H. pylori.
Tomar PPI 30 min antes de la comida y no interrumpir el tratamiento.
Abstenerse de alcohol, tabaco y alimentos irritantes (café, cítricos, chocolate).
Reconocer signos de sangrado (hematemesis, melena) y buscar atención inmediata.
Seguir dieta ligera y fraccionada durante la curación.

evidenced_by: alivio parcial con alimentos o antiácidos
puntaje de dolor ≥4 en escala de 0‑10
outcomes: Control del dolor: puntaje ≤3 en escala de 0‑10 en 48 h
Tolerancia a la dieta blanda sin aumento del dolor en 72 h

interventions.action: Evaluar dolor cada 2 h usando escala numérica y registrar patrón.
interventions.rationale: Permite medir la efectividad del tratamiento y ajustar intervenciones.

interventions.action: Administrar inhibidor de bomba de protones según prescripción y observar respuesta.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la secreción ácida y favorece la cicatrización de la úlcera.

interventions.action: Ofrecer antiácidos de acción rápida cuando el dolor sea intenso.
interventions.rationale: Alivia rápidamente la irritación ácida mientras actúan los PPI.

interventions.action: Enseñar al paciente técnicas de relajación y respiración profunda.
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la percepción del dolor y el estrés asociado.

interventions.action: Revisar y registrar ingesta de alimentos y relación con el dolor.
interventions.rationale: Identifica desencadenantes y ayuda a planificar la dieta.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Volumen intravascular mantenido; presión arterial estable (≥90 mmHg sistólica) en 72 h
Peso corporal sin pérdida >2 % en 72 h

interventions.action: Monitorear ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 4 h; registrar balance hídrico.
interventions.rationale: Detecta pérdidas ocultas y permite reposición oportuna.

interventions.action: Obtener hemograma y niveles de hemoglobina cada 24 h mientras haya sangrado.
interventions.rationale: Evalúa la magnitud de la pérdida sanguínea y la necesidad de transfusión.

interventions.action: Administrar solución cristaloide (ej. NaCl 0.9 %) según orden para mantener perfusión.
interventions.rationale: Reemplaza el volumen perdido y previene hipotensión.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de sangrado (hematemesis, melena) y cuándo buscar ayuda.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección temprana y la intervención rápida.

interventions.action: Revisar y suspender el uso de AINEs; ofrecer alternativas analgésicas.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la causa subyacente de daño mucoso y pérdida de líquidos.

en.summary: Erosive lesion of the gastric or duodenal mucosa caused by an imbalance between acid aggression and mucosal defense.
key_points: H. pylori and NSAIDs are the most common causes.
Typical epigastric pain worsens between meals or at night.
Diagnosis: endoscopy and tests for H. pylori.
Treatment: proton pump inhibitors + antibiotic eradication.
Severe complications: bleeding, perforation, and obstruction.

pathophysiology: Excess acid overwhelms the protective mucosal barrier.
H. pylori produces urease that damages epithelium and increases inflammation.
NSAIDs inhibit prostaglandins, reduce bicarbonate secretion and mucosal blood flow.
Chronic damage leads to erosion and ulcer formation.
signs_symptoms: Burning epigastric pain, worse between meals or at night.
Nausea and vomiting, sometimes with blood (hematemesis).
diagnostics: Upper GI endoscopy: visualizes ulcer and allows biopsy.
Urea breath test for H. pylori (positive).
Stool antigen test for H. pylori.
treatment: Antibiotics for eradication: amoxicillin + clarithromycin ± metronidazole.
Discontinue NSAIDs; use acetaminophen as analgesic.
nursing_care: Assess pain (intensity, relation to food and rest).
Monitor vital signs, blood pressure and heart rate.
Check hemoglobin, hematocrit and signs of bleeding.
Administer PPI as ordered and observe adverse effects.
Maintain NPO pre‑endoscopy; start a bland diet post‑procedure.
Position patient semi‑upright to reduce reflux.
patient_teaching: Avoid NSAIDs; prefer acetaminophen for pain.
Complete the antibiotic regimen to eradicate H. pylori.
Take PPI 30 min before meals and do not discontinue treatment.
Avoid alcohol, tobacco and irritating foods (coffee, citrus, chocolate).
Recognize signs of bleeding (hematemesis, melena) and seek immediate care.
Follow a light, divided diet during healing.

evidenced_by: partial relief with food or antacids
outcomes: Pain control: score ≤3 on 0‑10 scale within 48 h
Tolerate bland diet without increased pain within 72 h

interventions.action: Assess pain every 2 h using a numeric scale and record pattern.
interventions.rationale: Allows measurement of treatment effectiveness and adjustment of interventions.

interventions.action: Administer proton pump inhibitor as prescribed and observe response.
interventions.rationale: Reduces acid secretion and promotes ulcer healing.

interventions.action: Offer rapid‑acting antacids when pain is intense.
interventions.rationale: Provides quick relief of acid irritation while PPIs take effect.

interventions.action: Teach patient relaxation and deep‑breathing techniques.
interventions.rationale: Reduces pain perception and associated stress.

interventions.action: Review and record food intake and its relation to pain.
interventions.rationale: Identifies triggers and aids diet planning.

outcomes: Maintain intravascular volume; blood pressure stable (≥90 mmHg systolic) within 72 h

interventions.action: Monitor intake and output every 4 h; record fluid balance.
interventions.rationale: Detects hidden losses and allows timely replacement.

interventions.action: Obtain CBC and hemoglobin levels every 24 h while bleeding persists.
interventions.rationale: Assesses magnitude of blood loss and need for transfusion.

interventions.action: Administer crystalloid solution (e.g., 0.9 % NaCl) as ordered to maintain perfusion.
interventions.rationale: Replaces lost volume and prevents hypotension.

interventions.action: Educate patient on signs of bleeding (hematemesis, melena) and when to seek help.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection and rapid intervention.

interventions.action: Review and discontinue NSAID use; offer alternative analgesics.
interventions.rationale: Reduces underlying mucosal damage and fluid loss.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Histamine Blockers and Proton-Pump Inhibitors

key_points.0.quote: The most common cause is infection with a bacterium called Helicobacter pylori .

key_points.1.quote: The pain: Starts between meals or during the night

key_points.2.quote: Your doctor also may look inside your stomach and duodenum by doing an endoscopy or x-ray.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: The most common cause is infection with a bacterium called Helicobacter pylori .

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Another cause is the long-term use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (NSAIDs) such as aspirin and ibuprofen.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Not smoking and avoiding alcohol can help.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: A burning stomach pain is the most common symptom.

sections.treatment.0.quote: Omeprazole is the prototype antisecretory PPI that suppresses the secretion of gastric acid by inhibiting the gastric proton pump found within the parietal cells.

sections.complications.3.quote: Therefore, they prevent or treat heartburn, acid indigestion, gastric and duodenal ulcers, GERD, and hypersecretory conditions such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome .

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Assess blood pressure, heart rate, electrocardiogram, respiratory status, and changes in urine and bowel elimination.
